proposals.before: After he killed Xizong, he sent for Prince of Ge Zong Min.
proposals.after: After he killed Xizong, he had the Prince of Ge summon Zong Min.
proposals.reason: Chinese 使葛王宗敏 means sending the Prince of Ge to fetch Zong Min; the English fuses two people.

proposals.before: Kexi was fierce in battle beyond others, cruel and eager for disorder; a grandson of Taizu in the yi line, he nursed no small designs.
proposals.after: Kexi was fierce in battle beyond others, cruel and eager for disorder; as a grandson of Taizu, he nursed no small designs.
proposals.reason: 自乙太祖孫 is almost certainly 自以太祖孫; yi line is not meaningful.

proposals.before: In the twenty-third year, Shuang's illness lingered. An edict instructed the offices: "When Prince Rong's mourning leave reaches one hundred days, he shall receive a prince's stipend."
proposals.after: In the twenty-third year, Shuang's illness lingered. An edict instructed the offices: "When Prince Rong's sick leave reaches one hundred days, he shall receive a prince's stipend."
proposals.reason: 告 here is sick leave, not mourning; idiomatic already correct.

decisions.reason: s0096 使葛王宗敏, with s0097 identifying 葛王 as Shizong's first title and s0098 treating 宗敏 as a separate person summoned by Hailing, shows two people; the idiomatic wrongly fuses them, and separating Ge Wang as the agent who summons Zong Min matches the Chinese.
Chapter 自乙太祖孫 yields no meaningful 'yi line'; CText Jinshi ch. 69 reads 自以太祖孫 ('regarding himself as Taizu's grandson'), so dropping the invented lineage phrase is the correct repair.
s0037 opens with 爽疾久不愈 and the edict 榮王告滿百日; 告 here is sick leave during lingering illness (death only at s0038 既薨), so 'mourning leave' is wrong and 'sick leave' is accurate.
